question: At p=1/2, does the frozen shortest/lexicographic residual-path map have an L-independent inverse-multiplicity bound?
claim_boundary: This study concerns only the frozen deterministic map on the canonical q=1 square. A growing preimage family rejects that map as a bounded-to-one coupling, but does not reject fractional transport, another deterministic selector, or midpoint decodability.

frozen_model.geometry: canonical square of every integer size L>=3
frozen_model.transport: the already frozen shortest residual crossing, then left-to-right, edge-index and vertex lexicographic tie rule
frozen_model.target_image: j_star has current 1 on every horizontal edge and 0 on every vertical edge
frozen_model.candidate_preimages: for each row r, j_r is j_star with exactly that row's horizontal crossing toggled

competing_outcomes.uniform_bound: Every image has at most C preimages for one L-independent constant C.
competing_outcomes.counterfamily: The single image j_star has at least L distinct preimages j_r, disproving every L-independent bound.

proof_obligations: Each row crossing is a residual left-to-right path of length L-1 in j_r.
Every rough-to-rough path has length at least L-1.
Although j_r has right-to-left row crossings of the same length, the frozen direction tie rule selects the left-to-right row r.
T(j_r)=j_star for all r, and the j_r are distinct.
verification: Replay the construction only at the already audited L=3,4 controls; do not enumerate a new size.

acceptance.counterfamily: A proof valid for all L>=3 plus exact L3/L4 replay with zero construction, selector, image, charge, or logical failures.
acceptance.uniform_bound: An explicit L-independent bound proved for every image; finite L3/L4 maxima alone are insufficient.

stop_rule: Stop once one analytic outcome is proved and replayed on L3/L4. Do not tune the selector or test L>=5.
outcome: For every L>=3, the all-horizontal-left target j_star has at least L distinct row preimages under the frozen rule. Therefore maximum inverse multiplicity is at least L and no size-independent bound exists. Exact L3/L4 replay has zero failures.
